taxonomy_note: Treat Fleischmannia incarnata as the accepted species concept (FNA/POWO). Do not equate all pink Eupatorieae or cross-label Chromolaena odorata and Conoclinium coelestinum photographs.

project_inclusion.range_basis: FNA and NPSOT acknowledge species in Texas, but 3 target-zone counties are not independently confirmed through BONAP/NAPA; learner source-pool inclusion is independent of range certification.

look_here_first: Check a fully opened FLOWERING SHOOT and an OPPOSITE mature leaf: this is a lax/sprawling herb with paired triangular-to-heart-based COARSELY TOOTHED leaves on long petioles and loose sprays of relatively small pale-pink/purple discoid heads. To separate fragrant mistflower (Chromolaena odorata), view ONE flower head FROM THE SIDE: Fleischmannia's involucre is only ~4–5 mm long and has fewer overlapping phyllary series; Chromolaena usually has an 8–10 mm cylindrical involucre with many imbricated phyllaries. Blue mistflower (Conoclinium coelestinum) has many more florets/head and a distinctly conical receptacle; dissection helps. Color alone proves nothing.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial herb 30–120(–200) cm, lax or sprawling, weakly climbing or leaning among neighbors, much branched.
morphology_keys.stems: Herbaceous, often long and slender with widely spaced opposite leaves; do not confuse scrambling habit with twining vine.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, long-petiolate blades triangular-deltate, commonly 2–5(–7) × 1.5–3.5(–5) cm, base truncate to cordate, margins crenate-serrate/coarsely serrate. Look for the actual paired leaf bases at a node.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Small heads borne in relatively open flat-topped to irregular terminal corymbiform arrays on slender branchlets.
morphology_keys.flowers: Discoid heads without ray florets; small pink, pale lavender, pink-white or occasionally whitish florets, often about 13–25 per head in regional accounts; count individual florets rather than whole cluster.
morphology_keys.involucre: About 4–5 mm long, with comparatively few phyllary series; measure a SIDE VIEW next to a ruler, not the entire pink top.
morphology_keys.receptacle: Flat to slightly convex after florets are carefully removed (Conoclinium tends conspicuously conic). This is a diagnostic DISSECTION character, not typically visible in casual images.
morphology_keys.fruit: Cypselae about 1.8–2.8 mm in FNA, sparsely hairy to sometimes nearly smooth; pappus bristles. Microscopic carpopodium stopper-shaped and sharply differentiated.
field_id_sequence: Check opposite leaves on a single stem, including long petioles, toothed edge and triangular/heart-shaped base.
Trace the thin often sprawling herbaceous stems to small open branching clusters.
Photograph a whole inflorescence and then ONE individual head from the SIDE with scale.
Compare ~4–5 mm head involucre and bract ranks against longer ~8–10 mm cylindrical Chromolaena involucres.
If comparing to blue mistflower, count florets per head or carefully dissect a spent head for flat versus conic receptacle.
cautions: Pink heads plus opposite leaves are shared by Chromolaena, Conoclinium, and other eupatorieae; never identify by pink color alone.
Stem laxness and flower color vary across seasons and sites; use capitulum structure for final separation.
Currently installed photo views show field habit, foliage and head clusters but NOT a same-scale diagnostic involucre or receptacle macro; reserve arrows until a verified close-up is available.
Preserve UNRESOLVED county-native status until BONAP/NAPA target-zone county audit.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Chromolaena odorata (fragrant mistflower): larger ~8–10 mm long cylindrical involucres with many overlapping bract ranks vs Fleischmannia ~4–5 mm shorter heads; both can have toothed opposite leaves and pinkish flowers. Conoclinium coelestinum (blue mistflower): generally more disk florets (often 35–70+) per head and distinctly conic receptacle vs Fleischmannia ~13–25 and flat/slightly convex receptacle; flower shades overlap. Ageratina havanensis: usually woody/shrubby with white to lavender heads; confirm head architecture; no color-only ID.
